post.description:
Confirm actual cost for the authority that funded one served call.

The body names EXACTLY ONE funding source (wire-enforced): a
``reservation_id`` from the legacy per-call check, or the ``lease_id`` the
call drew its tokens from. A lease-funded confirm has no reservation to look
up — the lease itself is the ownership proof, bound to the caller's project
inside the settlement — so it skips the reservation choreography entirely.

``body.provider`` and ``body.is_provider_fallback`` are the *served*
failover attribution. They are accepted but **not persisted here** — the
durable served attribution is written via the metadata-ingest path onto
``cost_events`` (see ``metadata_ingest._store_cost_event``). Confirm only
settles the Redis budget counter, so it has nothing to attribute them to.

post.description:
Batch ingest metadata events from SDK instances (D16).

Resolves the project from the authenticated API key, deduplicates,
and stores events as CostEvent records. Max batch size: 1000 events.

Returns 202 for every well-formed request with per-event dispositions:
events the API refuses (unknown model, unknown service tier) appear in
``rejected`` while accepted events commit — a rejected event never
costs the rest of the batch.

Three populations share the 200: a GRANT, an INELIGIBLE answer (the run uses

BudgetConfirmRequest.title: BudgetConfirmRequest
BudgetConfirmRequest.description:
Post-call budget confirmation sent after an LLM call completes.

Ties one call's actual token usage to the authority that funded it so the
API can compute the exact cost via PricingService and settle it.

A call draws on EXACTLY ONE funding source, so exactly one of the two ids
is set (PJ-2):

* ``reservation_id`` — the legacy per-call path: the pre-flight check
  reserved an estimate, and this confirm trues it up.
* ``lease_id`` — the run held a budget LEASE and drew the call from the
  granted tokens, so there is no per-call reservation to settle. The server
  folds the actual cost into the lease's settled total and moves the
  enforcement counters only for spend that overshoots the lease's claim.

Naming both would settle the same call against one budget twice; naming
neither leaves nothing to settle.

LeaseGrantResponse.title: LeaseGrantResponse
LeaseGrantResponse.description:
Grant and renew response — one shape, three populations.

* INELIGIBLE (``eligible=False``): the run takes the legacy per-call path;
  no lease block.
* DENY (``allowed=False``): an authoritative hard-deny verdict feeding the
  SDK's existing sticky-deny machinery; no lease block.
* GRANT: the lease block is present. ``granted_tokens`` may be 0 (an
  alert_only project past its cap) — admission then falls to the legacy
  per-call path for each call without the run becoming ineligible.

The display snapshot at the bottom is always present so the SDK can log a
last-known budget position on any of the three.

MediaUsage.title: MediaUsage
MediaUsage.description:
Observable non-text billing quantities, measured inside the SDK firewall.

Billing rule: the SDK sends EVERY observable billing basis it can measure
from the request/response — WITHOUT ever reading prompt
or media content — and the SERVER's pricing-card unit (matched against the
dataset card's ``PriceVariant`` grid) selects WHICH single quantity prices
the call. A quantity is ``None`` when it is unobservable for that call —
never zero-as-default — so an unpriceable call routes to the server's
``is_unpriced`` lane instead of being billed as zero.

Why this model exists: OpenAI-compatible/Together image endpoints return
``usage: null``, so token counts are absent; for those calls these
request-derived quantities are the ONLY billing signal (verified against live
responses, 2026-07-10).

ProviderName.title: ProviderName
ProviderName.description:
Supported LLM provider identifiers.

The first four are native API dialects (Bedrock's Converse API is its
own dialect). The rest are OpenAI-compatible providers: they speak the
Chat Completions dialect but are distinct providers for attribution,
pricing, budget enforcement, and circuit breaking. ``OPENAI_COMPATIBLE``
is the generic catch-all for any unrecognized OpenAI-compatible endpoint
(custom proxies, new vendors).

Wire contract: these values ride MetadataEvent/BudgetCheckRequest/
BudgetConfirmRequest. The Cloud API must accept every value here BEFORE
an SDK carrying it is released (API deploys first) — keep lock-step with
the SDK's vendored ``solwyn._types.ProviderName``.

False for provider-reported counts. Wire shape: the SDK OMITS the key when False, so key-absent means provider-reported.

TokenDetails.title: TokenDetails
TokenDetails.description:
Normalized token usage breakdown for one LLM call.

Provider adapters populate whichever fields their API exposes; the rest
stay at 0.  The API uses this struct to compute exact costs rather than
trusting SDK-side estimates.

Normalization contract: ``input_tokens`` includes uncached input, cached
input reads, and cache-creation writes.  PricingService subtracts cached
buckets from ``input_tokens`` to derive uncached input, so provider adapters
must not send "uncached only" input totals.

Nesting contract: ``image_input_tokens`` is a SUBSET of ``input_tokens`` and
``image_output_tokens`` a SUBSET of ``output_tokens`` (probed live 2026-07-10:
an images.edit response reported input_tokens=222 with image_tokens=194 in
``input_tokens_details``). These mirror the existing ``reasoning_tokens`` ⊂
``output_tokens`` relationship — DOCUMENTED semantics, NOT validator-enforced
(reasoning is likewise unenforced). The only enforced subset invariant is the
cache-bucket one below; image tokens deliberately do not participate in it.
